name: Dull Indian Purple
lede: Dull Indian Purple is a muted, greyish mauve-purple from Robert Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature, one of several colors in his system carrying the modifier "Indian" without a stated reason.

sections.title: One of Ridgway's unexplained 'Indian' names
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature places this hue on plate XLIV, hue 69 triple-prime, tone i, and the ISCC-NBS system later classified it as a grayish reddish purple, about 5.2 units from that block's reference color [1]. Ridgway's book does not explain what "Indian" refers to across its various purple, red and yellow entries, so whether this name points to India, to a pigment once imported from there, or to some other convention is undocumented here [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[slate-purple]], [[deep-purplish-vinaceous]], [[old-lavender]] and [[deep-livid-brown]], at 3.7, 4.6, 
In Munsell terms this chip reads 6.3RP 4.4/2.9, low in chroma, the "dull" announced in its own name [1]. [[plum|Plum]] sits closer in hue, if not in our measured distance [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to this color in 70 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.29 percent, and in 31 by the stricter within-painting measure, which makes it rarer than 57 percent of the named colors we track [2]. Inside those paintings it most often sits as a hidden color, 58 percent of the 31, present but not dominant, the kind of tone a varnish layer can mute further [2]. It is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 3.1 times the expected rate, 8 of 721 such paintings, and peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 2.5 times expected [2].

The earliest match in our archive dates to 1450, with the latest from 1932, 46 dated paintings in all, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. That earliest match is 462 years before the name's own earliest record in our sources, 1912 [1][2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].

openers: Dull Indian Purple is one of three "Indian"-named colors in our library, and none of the three come with an explanation.
In our archive, this muted purple shows up most often as a hidden color -- present, but never the star of the canvas.
